title: Screen reader basics and landmarks
learningObjectives: Explain screen reader basics and landmarks and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Screen readers expose semantic structure, accessible names, roles, states, and content through speech or braille output. Landmarks and heading levels provide navigation shortcuts. Native semantics should be preferred over recreating roles with generic elements.
understand.whyItMatters: A page can look correct while its structure is confusing when announced. Test with a screen reader and ensure names and state match the visible interface.
understand.analogy: A screen reader provides an alternate map and spoken route through the page's structure.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The main landmark, named navigation, and heading hierarchy provide structural navigation points.
